data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The problem is a category error: 'safe' and 'idempotent' as defined in RFC 9110 are properties of HTTP request methods, not of arbitrary log-writer operations. The log does not require either property in the RFC sense. Instead, it requires 'at-least-once tolerance' \u2014 a property not named in the RFCs but constructible from first principles: the writer's effect on the log must be a pure function of the intended event, not of the delivery count. This is structurally identical to idempotency but should not be conflated with the RFC definition because the operational context (log appends, not HTTP requests) is different.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the problem explicitly asks for 'published definitions' and intends RFC 9110, refusing to use them may miss the expected answer.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the log writers are literally HTTP clients using PUT/POST to an HTTP-accessible log API, the RFC definitions may apply directly after all.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If 'safe' refers to the distributed-systems safety-property definition (Lamport), the category-error argument doesn't hold.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"RFC 9110's definitions are scoped to HTTP methods and their effects on 'the origin server.' An append-only event log's writers are not HTTP methods (even if they use HTTP as a transport). The relevant property is: given an intended event e, the log after delivering e exactly once equals the log after delivering e k times (for any k \u2265 1). Call this 'delivery-idempotency.' It is analogous to RFC idempotency but defined over the delivery channel, not the HTTP method. The log requires delivery-idempotency of its writers. Safety in the RFC sense (no side effects) is irrelevant because the writer's entire purpose is to produce a side effect (an append). The distinction that matters is between delivery-idempotency (which the log needs) and operational safety/crash-resistance (which the log infrastructure provides, not the writer).","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
